name: the Bois de Vincennes
title: Ancient Trees in the Bois de Vincennes, Paris: 5 to Find
meta_description: Planes planted five years before their island, a walnut older than its lake, and twin planes at the chateau. Five trees in the Bois de Vincennes.
intro: By the city's own dates, the planes of the Ile de Bercy are five years older than the island they stand on. The register gives all five a planting year of 1860, and the island was made in 1865, when Lac Daumesnil was dug out of the Bois de Vincennes. A black walnut beside the same lake is older still, planted in 1845, twenty years before the water, and it grew as a clump that started out as three stems. A lakeside London plane with a planting year of 1871 is wider than any of the Bercy planes, at 530 centimetres round. In front of the Chateau de Vincennes, two planes put in the ground in 1918 are 34 and 35 metres tall, with trunks the register measures at 635 and 630 centimetres, figures worth a second look for trees so young. Across the square, a weeping beech dated 1864 or 1865 is older than Square Carnot itself, a dome you walk around rather than look up at.
